result: The authors obtained high-resolution cryoEM structures of Kv1.2 in four different states: open (3.2 Å), C-type inactivated (2.5 Å), DTx-bound (3.2 Å), and K+-free/Na+-bound (2.9 Å), all at nominally zero membrane potential in detergent micelles.
evaluation: All reviewers explicitly acknowledge the high-resolution structures obtained. Reviewer 1 states 'the quality of the structural data presented in this revised manuscript is very high and allows for unambiguous assignment of side chains.' Reviewer 3 notes the structures are 'well-executed' and commends 'the breadth of the studies.' The resolutions and experimental conditions are not questioned by any reviewer.

result: The Kv1.2 structure is very similar to Shaker and Kv1.2-2.1 chimera structures, with 68% amino-acid identity to Shaker and an RMS difference of 0.85 Å for VSD Arg sidechain atoms, and shows an open S6 gate as expected.
evaluation: Reviewer 3 notes that 'the findings are mostly confirmatory' regarding the open structure, implicitly accepting the structural similarity claims. No reviewer challenges the quantitative measurements or structural comparisons presented. The confirmatory nature is acknowledged without dispute.

result: The W366F mutant of Kv1.2 shows rapid C-type inactivation with currents decaying to <3% within 80ms, and the structure reveals a large expansion of the selectivity filter with Y28' reorienting ~120°, enlarging IS2 to 5.1 Å and IS1 to 11 Å, with no clear ion densities in the upper filter but strong densities in IS3 and IS4, maintaining C4 symmetry.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 states 'One of the main findings is the determination of the structure of a mutant (W366F) that is thought to correspond to the slow inactivated state. These experiments confirm results in similar mutants in different channels from Kv1.2 that indicate that inactivation is associated with an enlarged selectivity filter.' Reviewer 3 acknowledges these are 'mostly confirmatory' but does not challenge the structural details or measurements.

result: The VSD shows minimal changes between open and inactivated states at the S4-S5 interface (<1 Å), but exhibits a ~3° rotation at the bottom with helices S0, S1, and S2 tilting by 6°, 4°, and 3.2° respectively, a feature not observed in Shaker or Kv1.2-2.1 structures.
evaluation: No reviewer challenges these structural observations about VSD movements. The detailed quantitative measurements are presented without dispute. Reviewer 1 notes 'the quality of the structural data presented in this revised manuscript is very high,' supporting the reliability of these observations.

result: α-Dendrotoxin blocks Kv1.2 by attaching to the negatively-charged outer mouth via three salt bridges, with its Lys5 residue penetrating into the selectivity filter and the terminal amine coordinated by Y17' carbonyls, resulting in only two ion densities (in IS1 and IS3) rather than three as in other toxin-blocked channels.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 states 'Another interesting structure is the complex of Kv1.2 with the pore blocking toxin Dendrotoxin 1. The results shown in the revised version indicate that the mechanism of block is similar to that of related blocking-toxins, in which a lysine residue penetrates in the pore. Surprisingly, in these new structures, the bound toxin results in a pore with empty external potassium binding sites.' Reviewer 2 notes 'The new findings from a further analysis of the toxin channel complex are welcome information on the mode of the binding of dendrotoxin.' Reviewer 3 states 'The DTx structure has been markedly improved in the revised version and the authors arrive at well-founded conclusions regarding its mechanism of block.'

result: No toxin binding was observed when α-DTX was mixed with the inactivated W366F mutant, suggesting the toxin cannot bind to the inactivated conformation.
evaluation: This negative result is presented as part of the toxin binding studies and is not challenged by any reviewer. It supports the interpretation that toxin binding requires a specific selectivity filter conformation.

result: The structure of Kv1.2 in Na+ solution shows an intact selectivity filter with ion density in each binding site, essentially identical to the K+-bound structure, though Na+ and K+ ions cannot be distinguished in the density maps.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 states 'the structures of the dendrotoxin bound Kv1.2 and the channel in Na+ are new findings that will of interest to the general channel community.' Reviewer 3 notes 'the authors present structures of DTx-bound Kv1.2 and of Kv1.2 in a low concentration of potassium (which may contain sodium ions bound within the selectivity filter). These two structures add considerable new information.' The limitation regarding ion discrimination is acknowledged by the authors and not disputed.

result: The W366F mutant in Na+ solution showed highly variable conformation allowing only low-resolution structure determination, suggesting the channel has a highly unstable conformation when K+ ions are absent.
evaluation: This observation is presented as a negative result explaining why high-resolution structure could not be obtained. No reviewer challenges this interpretation or the experimental observation.

result: The manuscript provides extensive background on potassium channel selectivity filter structure, C-type inactivation mechanisms, and the role of key residues like Y28' and D30' in maintaining filter stability, citing established literature.
evaluation: These are background claims citing established literature. No reviewer challenges the accuracy of these citations or the background information provided. They serve as context for the new findings.

result: The manuscript discusses selectivity filter expansion in W17'F mutants across multiple channels (Shaker, Kv1.2-2.1, Kv1.2), ion occupancy patterns, functional properties, and comparisons with other inactivated structures including Kv1.3 conformations.
evaluation: These comparative analyses and literature discussions are presented to contextualize the findings. Reviewer 3 notes 'Although the findings are mostly confirmatory, they do add to the body of work on this and related channels,' implicitly accepting these comparisons as valid context.

result: The manuscript discusses various toxin blocking mechanisms in potassium channels, including spider toxins, cone-snail toxins, charybdotoxin, and ShK, and notes that Leu9 substitution reduces α-DTX affinity 1000-fold despite showing no structural contacts.
evaluation: These are contextual claims citing established literature and making comparisons. No reviewer challenges these background discussions or the cited functional data.

result: The Kv1.2 transmembrane region conformation appears insensitive to lipid vs. detergent environment; the construct contains specific mutations in disordered regions and β2-subunits with charge-neutralizing mutations that don't affect structure, and α4 and α4β4 complexes were structurally indistinguishable.
evaluation: These methodological details and observations are presented without challenge from reviewers. Reviewer 1 notes 'the quality of the structural data presented in this revised manuscript is very high,' supporting the validity of these technical observations.

result: Despite closely matched VSD structures, gating charge movement differs between Shaker (~13 e0) and Kv1.2 (10 e0) channels.
evaluation: This observation citing published data is presented as a puzzling discrepancy. No reviewer challenges this comparison or the cited values.

result: The manuscript cites literature showing that KcsA selectivity filter collapses in low K+, while Shaker and Kv2.1 conduct Na+ in the absence of K+, and Shaker-W17'F carries large Na+ and Li+ currents without K+.
evaluation: These are literature citations providing context for the Na+ structure findings. No reviewer disputes these cited observations.
